transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been on edge. I snap at my wife over little things around the house, and I’ve been putting off jobs and paperwork I normally handle. Even when I go out to the workshop or try to fish, I can’t really quiet my head down.
How long ago did your father-in-law move in, and how long have you been feeling this on-edge and irritable since then?
It’s been about five months now. It started shortly after he moved into the house.
Aside from the tension at home with your father-in-law, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things too—like work, money, or your health—even when they're going fine?
I’m not sure I’d call it worrying about everything else. It mostly feels tied to what’s going on at home.
Besides feeling on edge, have you also been feeling down, sad, or hopeless, or noticed you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like fishing?
I’m not really sure. I know I’m more wound up than anything. Fishing doesn’t clear my head like it usually does, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt hopeless.
Besides feeling irritable, have you done things like yelling, breaking things, or acting out in ways that go against your usual behavior or cause trouble with others—at home or elsewhere?

I’ve been snapping at my wife over little things around the house, which isn’t like me. I haven’t broken anything or anything like that, but I’ve also been putting off jobs and paperwork I normally keep up with.
Have you done anything like getting into physical altercations, breaking rules at work, or running into trouble with authorities since this all started?
No, nothing like that. I’ve been irritable at home, but I haven’t gotten physical with anyone or had trouble with the police or anything.
When you feel this on-edge tension building up, do you also notice physical signs like your heart racing, muscles feeling tight, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed those kinds of physical things. It’s more just that I feel keyed up.
Since your father-in-law moved in, have there been times you've felt sad, tearful, or down about things, even briefly, apart from feeling irritable or on edge?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve been more on edge, but I haven’t particularly noticed feeling sad or tearful.
Besides fishing feeling different, have you noticed less interest or enjoyment in other activities or things you used to look forward to since your father-in-law moved in?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed that, no. Other than fishing feeling different, I can’t really think of other things I’ve stopped enjoying.
When you feel this on-edge and keyed up, would you describe it more as feeling nervous or anxious, or is it hard to put a specific label on the feeling?
It’s hard to label exactly. I just can’t seem to get my head quiet, even when I’m out in the workshop or trying to fish.
